title: Projective compactification of an affine piece
statement:
Let $S$ be Noetherian, let $U$ be an affine scheme with a morphism $U\to S$
of finite type, and let $\iota:U\to\mathbf A^n_S$ be an immersion over $S$
(as supplied by [def-nagata-quasi-affine-immersion-affine-space]). Let
$\overline U\subseteq\mathbf P^n_S$ be the scheme-theoretic image of the
composite immersion $U\xrightarrow{\iota}\mathbf A^n_S\hookrightarrow
\mathbf P^n_S$. Then $\overline U$ is a closed subscheme of
$\mathbf P^n_S$, so $\overline U\to S$ is projective and in particular
proper, and $U\to\overline U$ is a quasi-compact, scheme-theoretically dense
open immersion. Thus $U\to\overline U\to S$ is a dense projective
compactification of $U\to S$.

proof.text: Write $f:U\to S$ for the given morphism and $P=\mathbf P^n_S=\mathbf P(\{0,\ldots,n\};S)$. By [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion], the standard chart $a:\mathbf A^n_S\hookrightarrow P$ is an open immersion over $S$. Set $\kappa=a\circ\iota$. Thus $\pi\circ\kappa=f$, where $\pi:P\to S$ is the structure morphism. The homogeneous-coordinate index set has $n+1$ elements, including when $n=0$.

source.place: standard-chart composite in the statement; current standard-chart lemma, extra homogeneous coordinate

proof.text: By the definition of immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], factor $\iota$ as a closed immersion $U\hookrightarrow V$ followed by an open immersion $V\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_S$. The composite $V\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_S\xrightarrow{a}P$ identifies $V$ with an open subscheme of the open chart of $P$: an open subset of an open subset is open and restriction of the structure sheaf is transitive [def-weil-open-immersion]. Therefore $\kappa$ is a closed immersion followed by an open immersion, hence an immersion.

source.place: Tag 01IO (definition-immersion), and elementary open-immersion case of Tag 02V0 (lemma-composition-immersion)

proof.text: The structure morphism $\pi$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], applied to the finite homogeneous-coordinate set $\{0,\ldots,n\}$. In particular it is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target] to $U\xrightarrow{\kappa}P\xrightarrow{\pi}S$: the composite is $f$, of finite type by hypothesis, and the second morphism is separated. Hence $\kappa$ is of finite type, and therefore quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This proves precisely the hypothesis needed for the image lemma without any assertion about arbitrary morphisms out of $U$.

source.place: statement and graph-factorization proof; proper projective-space projection from the current blueprint

proof.text: Apply [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc] to $\kappa$. Its image $\overline U=\operatorname{SIm}(\kappa)$ is a closed subscheme of $P$, with closed immersion $c:\overline U\hookrightarrow P$ and canonical factor $j:U\to\overline U$. The canonical factorization [def-nagata-scheme-image-factor] satisfies $c\circ j=\kappa$. All these objects are those of the statement, rather than a reduced topological closure.

source.place: Tags 01R7 (definition-scheme-theoretic-image), 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image); current blueprint image-interface and canonical-factor nodes

proof.text: Now $\kappa$ is both an immersion (step 2) and quasi-compact (step 3). Thus [lemma-nagata-immersion-open-in-scheme-image] applies to this very morphism and says that $j:U\to\overline U$ is a quasi-compact open immersion with scheme-theoretically dense image (also topologically dense). No reducedness hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tag 01RG (lemma-quasi-compact-immersion), quasi-compact alternative; quasi-compactness of the canonical factor supplied by the cited node

proof.text: Set $p=\pi\circ c:\overline U\to S$. The inclusion $c$ is a closed immersion and $\pi$ is proper by step 3. Clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] therefore proves that $p$ is proper. In particular $p$ is of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

The closed immersion $c:\overline U\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_S$ and the equality $p=\pi\circ c$ give an H-projective presentation of $p$. Together with its quasi-compactness from step 6, these are exactly the two requirements in [def-pc-projective-morphism]. Thus $p$ is projective in the blueprint convention.

source.place: Tag 01W8 (definition-projective), H-projective clause; blueprint convention also requires quasi-compactness

proof.text: Finally $p\circ j=\pi\circ c\circ j=\pi\circ\kappa=f$. Step 5 gives the quasi-compact open immersion and schematic density; step 6 gives properness and step 7 gives projectivity. The factorization is therefore a compactification in the sense of [def-nagata-compactification], with the additional quasi-compactness, density and projectivity claimed in the statement.

proof_origin.place: proof, Steps 1-3 (quasi-compact immersion; closure; projectivity), with the quasi-compactness of Step 1 obtained from the finite-type cancellation lemma instead of the uncited Noetherian-source claim, and the closed-immersion properness and projectivity made explicit
